cases.title: Polymorphic indexed vector map with nil and cons equations
cases.prelude:
inductive RecursionVec (A : Type) : Nat → Type where
  | nil : RecursionVec A 0
  | cons {n : Nat} : A → RecursionVec A n → RecursionVec A (n + 1)
cases.type: ∀ (A B : Type), (A → B) → ∀ n, RecursionVec A n → RecursionVec B n
cases.reference: fun A B g _ xs => let rec go {n : Nat} (ys : RecursionVec A n) : RecursionVec B n := match ys with | .nil => .nil | .cons x rest => .cons (g x) (go rest); go xs

kernel_checks.type: ∀ (A B : Type) (g : A → B), @{f} A B g 0 .nil = .nil
∀ (A B : Type) (g : A → B) (n : Nat) (x : A) (xs : RecursionVec A n), @{f} A B g (n + 1) (.cons x xs) = .cons (g x) (@{f} A B g n xs)

cases.replay: (match @{f} Nat Bool (fun n => n == 0) 3 (.cons 0 (.cons 7 (.cons 0 .nil))) with | .cons a (.cons b (.cons c .nil)) => a == true && b == false && c == true) = true ∧ (match @{f} Bool Nat (fun b => if b then 2 else 9) 3 (.cons false (.cons true (.cons false .nil))) with | .cons a (.cons b (.cons c .nil)) => a == 9 && b == 2 && c == 9) = true
cases.source: docs/proposals/new/1/sections/05-dependent.tex: ordinary Vec.map motive; fresh indexed datatype, independent constructor equations and executable values
